extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of literary criticism; scholars and educated general readers interested in poetry, Greek tragedy, and Shakespeare
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts evaluative principles the essays give for judging or producing poetry, Greek tragedy, and Shakespearean drama. Focuses on what counts as poeticness, tragic form, and dramatic greatness according to the authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irreducibility of poetic effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry is measured by 'the degree in which we feel it hopeless to convey the effect of a poem or passage in any form but its own.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the notion of translating a passage into other forms is 'simply ludicrous,' you have quintessential poetry. The more impossible it is to render in other language or art, the more truly poetic the passage is.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of form and substance
rubrics_metrics.description: The content and the form in poetry are one thing: 'the content is one thing with the form.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good poetry is not merely a preconceived matter clothed in metrical language. Beware 'merely decorative effect' where a poet 'clothed' a distinct truth in metrical diction; such decoration makes the poetry 'not wholly poetic.' The unity means meaning and expression are inseparable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of 'poetic diction' as mere phraseology
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Wordsworth inveighed against poetic diction' aimed at phraseology (the worn-out body of an old one), not the living body of new content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The formalist heresy treats form as separable and encourages tasting poetry as a fine wine with aesthetic but small value. That invites empty form filled with cheap pathos, sentiment, vulgar humour, lust, vanity. Criticize poetry that substitutes pretty phrasing for genuine content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry must originate in creative discovery ('pure poetry')
rubrics_metrics.description: Pure poetry 'springs from the creative impulse of a vague imaginative mass pressing for development and definition' — the poet often does not know the precise meaning until the poem is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the poet already knew exactly what he meant to say, the poem would be unnecessary. The compositional process reveals meaning; poems that are merely expressions of preconceived ideas lack the sense of creation and therefore the magical effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning-as-self: accept poems that 'mean themselves'
rubrics_metrics.description: For genuinely creative poems, when asked 'What does poetry mean?' the answer can only be 'It means itself.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insisting on a pre-digested paraphrase of a poem's meaning is mistaken; such poetry's meaning is unique to its own language and cannot be fully restated without loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry's suggestive, 'all-embracing' quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Best poetry 'floats an atmosphere of infinite suggestion' — the poet speaks of one thing that seems to 'beckon away beyond itself' and 'expand into something boundless.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This suggestive power is a large part of poetry's value; it may be found in both lofty tragedies and small children's songs. Evaluate poetry by its capacity to suggest wider, often spiritual or philosophical, resonances beyond the literal subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translatability limit: other arts only analogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Because poetry is in words we vainly imagine other words or arts can express the same meaning; but 'they will do so no more... only a little more' — other arts can give analogues but not the poem's own meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not judge a poem by whether prose or another art can convey the same sense; instead recognize the poem's irreplaceable mode of expression. Use analogues (music, painting, philosophy) only as aids, not substitutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not instrumentalize poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry 'is not our servant; it is our master.' It 'will not speak at our bidding, nor answer in our language.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist attempts to bend poetry to didactic or practical purposes. Treating poetry as a tool to serve other ends diminishes its dignity and unique effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate subject-matter for Greek tragedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Greek tragedy's subject must be taken from the cycle of legends familiar to the audience; scenes out of the lives of ancient heroes, chosen for edification as well as delight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The theme is strictly prescribed by religious festival context; whatever personal reflections a poet adds, they must be 'subservient to the main object' of setting forth episodes of heroic, semi-divine ancestry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tragic hero must be greater-than-ordinary and ethically complex
rubrics_metrics.description: The tragic hero is 'a man of high place and birth who having a nature not ignoble has fallen into sin and pays in suffering the penalty of his act.' A 'complete villain' or an 'absolutely good man' are not proper tragic subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aristotle's canon excludes purely bad or purely good figures because they fail to engage sympathy or to provide the proper pleasure of tragic art. The hero's mixture of greatness and fault is essential to tragedy's ethical-aesthetic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tragedy as interpretation with moral/aesthetic unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Greek tragedy is composed from a definite point of view with the aim not merely to represent but 'also to interpret the theme' — to illustrate some general moral law or fundamental truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elder dramatists like Aeschylus and Sophocles aimed to justify the ways of God to man or to justify law against presumption. The chorus often functions to state the moral and ensure the play's interpretive tone; moralizing is woven into the art rather than tacked on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on action and typicality over individual character development
rubrics_metrics.description: In Greek tragedy 'the interest was centred on the universal bearing of certain acts and situations' and 'the characters are broad and simple, not developing for the most part, but fixed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The drama represents 'human nature in the broad' using typical situations that illuminate general human or civic truths; avoid focusing on idiosyncratic psychological development as the primary aim in this idiom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and performance integral: chorus, music, dance, declamation
rubrics_metrics.description: Greek tragedy combines lyric odes, chorus, dance, music, masks, and statuesque declamation; 'the moving pageant ... set in tune with nature' and appeals to eye, ear, passion, and intellect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess tragedy by its integrated use of multiple arts—choral lyric that comments and sums moral meaning, actors' declamatory style, masks, and stage spectacle—rather than only by the written text. The form is 'admirably adapted' to the aim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of familiar mythic background for resonant allusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Because audiences knew the heroic cycles, a few allusive words could 'call into existence' the sombre background and enhance the terrors or meaning of current scenes (e.g., the House of Atreus in Agamemnon).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dramatic effectiveness often relies on invoking an established mythic history to create depth and inevitable doom; choose subjects that carry communal associative weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shakespearean greatness: cultural embodiment and portraiture
rubrics_metrics.description: Shakespeare 'embodies for us the Outer Life of our Europe' — chivalries, courtesies, humours, ambitions — and excels at 'portrait-painting, delineating of men and things, especially of men.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge Shakespearean drama by its capacity to record national life and to delineate characters with penetrating, calm insight. His power lies in selecting essentials, suppressing the irrelevant, and making an ordered, 'fit' dramatic whole from chaotic materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic construction: insight, selection, and organic unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Shakespeare's dramas show deliberate illumination: 'to find out which circumstance is vital and shall stand prominent; which unessential, fit to be suppressed... Does like join itself to like... so that its embroilment becomes order?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate dramatic works by structural coherence: choice of beginning, sequence, ending; the author's capacity to 'Fiat lux' — make light and order — and to fashion a complete, self-sufficient 'house' from raw materials.
